tagline.text: A Tanay hike with a sea of clouds and eight small waterfalls

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Cayabu, Tanay, Rizal (foothills of the Sierra Madre)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May (sea of clouds at dawn from February to June; avoid the June–October rainy season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600–1,300 (per person, covering transport, registration and a shared guide)

children.text: Mount Maynoba is a 728-meter mountain in Barangay Cayabu, Tanay, Rizal, and its loop route that links it with nearby Mount Cayabu is popular. You can enjoy a dawn sea of clouds, Sierra Madre views and eight waterfalls on the way down in half a day, making it a good day hike near Manila.

Mount Maynoba is a mountain in the Sierra Madre foothills of Tanay, Rizal. It is 728 meters high and the trailhead is in Barangay Cayabu. It became widely known among mountain enthusiasts when it officially opened in early 2016, and it is now often named as a mountain near Manila with a high chance of a sea of clouds. According to local guides, the name is said to come from a plant called "toba" (tuba) that once grew abundantly on the slopes. Some sources spell it Maynuba.
The route usually starts with Mount Cayabu (about

above sea level), which lies close to Maynoba, then follows the ridge to the Maynoba viewpoint and summit, descends through forest, passes eight small waterfalls and returns to the village. It is rated about 3 to 4 out of 9, so beginners can try it, but the initial climb up Mount Cayabu is the steepest part. From the summit side you are said to see Mount Tukduang Banoi and Mount Irid to the north, and ranges toward Tanay, Infanta and General Nakar to the east. The descent runs through forest and bamboo and follows a stream, and the rocky area near the waterfalls makes the final stretch surprisingly tricky. Some sections have ropes or railings, but they can be slippery when muddy, so do not rely on them and check your footing first. You can get water where the waterfall area begins, and leeches or rattan thorns are rarely reported.

The biggest attraction of Maynoba is the dawn sea of clouds. Some hiking sources rate it as having the highest chance of a sea of clouds among Rizal's mountains, but it is never guaranteed on any given day. One visitor reported seeing only clear scenery with no clouds in January. The sea of clouds is said to be best at 5:30–7:00 AM on the morning after light rain between February and June. To reach the ridge before sunrise you must leave Manila at 2–3 AM, so a private or chartered vehicle is more convenient.

This guide is for travelers planning a day hike from Manila. Even if you have little hiking experience, a guide is required and the route is well marked, so there is little worry about getting lost. The registration fee and guide fee at the trailhead differ slightly between sources and change over the years, so confirm them again on arrival. In the rainy season the trail is slippery with mud and the rocks around the waterfalls become dangerous, so it is better to avoid hiking then. Plan on 5–6 hours for the full loop, or 4–5 hours if you only go to the summit and back, and longer if you rest at the waterfalls. Contacts at the village entrance (the Barangay Cayabu office, a local guide coordinator and the Tanay tourism Facebook page) are listed in published sources, so it is easier to tell them your group size and date before you leave.

This is the first hurdle of the loop, a steep climb through thick forest. It takes the most energy at the start, but once you get past this section the ridge continues. Shorten your steps, drink water often and climb slowly.

From the viewpoint on the Maynoba ridge, the sea of clouds and the Sierra Madre ridgeline spread out. You must arrive at sunrise to see it before the clouds disappear. Some days you see it and some days you do not, so go with slightly lower expectations.
The upper section is an open grassy ridge with views in every direction, and the mountain ranges overlap one another. The summit is
high and usually takes
2–3 hours
from the trailhead. There is little shade, so you need a hat and sunscreen. On clear days at the summit you can pick out the northern and eastern ranges and get a sense of direction.

Small waterfalls 2–10 meters high follow one another along the stream on the way down. The names given in sources are Nagtatagong Paraiso, Katmon, Gugulong na Bato, Panat-in, Maypatak, Makapatak, Duyan and Maynuba Falls. Deep pools are good for swimming, but some spots are shallow, so follow your guide's instructions. Each fall has its own character, with spots to rest on mossy rocks, falls that pour as softly as rain and shallow places where children can play. The last, Maynuba Falls, is a good place to wash off the sweat before leaving the forest trail.
There is one campsite between Mount Cayabu and the Maynoba summit. Camping is reported at about
per tent, and showers cost extra. Groups who want to sleep over and see the dawn sea of clouds choose this.
Cayabu village has small stores, toilets, paid wash areas and parking. It is enough for washing off sweat and changing clothes after the descent, and you can buy light snacks and drinks.
You can add Masungi Georeserve (reservation required) on the way back to Manila after the hike. Doing both on the same day is tight, so splitting the schedule is more realistic.

children.text: Leave Manila by car, passing Marcos Highway, Antipolo, Baras and Sampaloc in Tanay.
Arrive in Barangay Cayabu, register and find a guide.
Start climbing Mount Cayabu. A headlamp is needed.
Rest at the Mount Cayabu summit and watch the sunrise.
Move to the Maynoba viewpoint and summit to see the sea of clouds and surrounding ranges.
Start the descent through forest trail and riverbed to the waterfall area.
Swim and rest at the waterfalls.
Return to the trailhead, wash up and set off for Manila.

This schedule assumes a private vehicle and changes with the sunrise position and the weather. On days without clouds, spend longer at the waterfalls instead. From November to January, when sunrise is later, the dawn is cold, so set out in a light jacket.
Take a jeepney to Cogeo from Cubao or EDSA.
Take a tricycle from the Batangasan junction to Cayabu village.
Register and climb with a guide.
Reach the summit viewpoint.
Descend and return to the trailhead.
Return to Manila by the same route.
Public transport makes it hard to match sunrise, so if the sea of clouds is your goal, a private or chartered vehicle is recommended. Check the first and last jeepney times locally.
Take a jeepney or UV Express to Cogeo Gate 2 in Antipolo from Cubao, EDSA or Aurora Boulevard. The fare is about
and the ride takes
30–45 minutes
From Cogeo Market (Padilla Terminal), take a jeepney to the Batangasan junction in Sampaloc, Tanay. The fare is about
and it takes
45 minutes to 1 hour
From the Batangasan junction, a tricycle to Cayabu village costs about
(varies by group size and season).
The total travel time is reported at 2–3 hours. Fares differ between the 2016 and 2025 sources, so confirm them locally.
Take Marcos Highway through Antipolo, Baras and Sampaloc in Tanay to Cayabu village.
There is parking at the trailhead.
If you leave around 2 AM, you can arrive before sunrise.
You can charter a van from Manila or use a day tour such as one sold on Klook.
Tours are sometimes reported to include round-trip transport, a guide and registration fees, so check what is included.
With a chartered van, the more people share it the lower the cost per person, and an early start is easier.
November to May is the comfortable hiking season. December–February is cool and good for walking, and February–June is reported to have a higher chance of a sea of clouds.

In the rainy season from June to October the trail is muddy and the rocks near the waterfalls are slippery and dangerous. Because the sea-of-clouds season in some sources (February–June) overlaps with the rainy season in June, decide on June by the weather.

On weekends and public holidays, guide assignment takes time and the summit viewpoint is crowded. A weekday dawn with fewer people is recommended, but the number of guides is limited even on weekdays, so groups should contact the village in advance.

Start early to avoid the sun and cool off at the waterfalls.
Mud and swollen streams are dangerous, so avoid hiking.

Cayabu village has small stores where you can buy water, snacks and cup noodles. There are no water refill points on the trail, so bring at least 2 liters per person. Lunch is usually a packed meal or snacks eaten while resting at the waterfalls. If you bring fruit, boiled eggs or rice balls bought at a market beforehand, they are light to carry, and you should take your trash back with you.

Day hikes are the norm, but if you want to camp, bring a tent, sleeping bag and headlamp and sleep at the campsite between Cayabu and Maynoba. If you need a room, hotels in Tanay town or Antipolo are the closest. If you camp, the dawn is cold so you need a light jacket, and you must carry out all your trash. Ask your guide in advance whether the village can provide a simple meal such as rice or noodles.
An early start is standard, so go to bed early the night before and bring a headlamp.
Wear hiking shoes or trekking sandals with good grip, and avoid light walking sneakers.
You can swim at the waterfalls, so bring a swimsuit, a quick-dry towel and a change of clothes.
Keep electronics in a waterproof bag.
Weekends are crowded, so a weekday or an early-dawn start is recommended.
A guide is required, and on foggy days especially follow their directions.
There are paid wash areas after the descent, so bring a change of clothes.
Hiking information mixes sources from 2016 to 2025, so confirm fees after you arrive.
Write your name and contact in the registration book, and tell your guide in advance if anyone in your group has a physical condition.
In the rainy season the trail is muddy and the rocks at the waterfalls are very slippery, so avoid the hike and always follow your guide's instructions.
If it rained heavily the day before, the stream can swell, so ask your guide whether to enter the waterfall section.
You cannot tell how deep the waterfall pools are, so do not jump in alone.
Mobile signal may only be available near the summit.
The summit section has almost no shade, so watch out for heat illness.
Hiking rules and fees change with village circumstances, so check Tanay tourism announcements.
A limestone-landscape conservation area you can reach by car from Cayabu village. Reservation is required.
Tanay's signature waterfall, a good place to rest after the hike.
A river and mountain trekking route in the same eastern part of Rizal.
